pin.note: npm dist-tags latest on 2026-11-25. The package is a thin launcher: platform binaries come as optional deps (@opencode/cli-linux-arm64, -musl variants). Install is 510 MB on linux-arm64; the runner image should npm ci from a lockfile.

install.note: The older opencode-ai line (npm latest 1.19.6) is not used.

credentialEnv.note: api_key (own endpoint) is the platform key the adapter sets as AGENTDESK_LLM_API_KEY; verified: provider config with env: ["AGENTDESK_LLM_API_KEY"] made the CLI send 'Authorization: Bearer <that value>' to the mock endpoint. auth_json has no env var: the pasted `opencode auth export` JSON is delivered as a file and loaded with `opencode auth import <file>` (or stdin).

home.note: There is no auth.json. Credentials live in the SQLite database opencode.db (table credential) under $XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode/, together with sessions. Config is read from $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode (default ~/.config/opencode), including plugins/ (auto-loaded) and service.json.

endpointNote: No env var. The address is the custom provider's options.baseURL in the config.
modelFlag: -m, --model <provider/model#variant> on `opencode run`; the TUI selects with the same config and its own picker.

noLogin.offers: opencode/* free models (opencode models lists 11, e.g. opencode/big-pickle, opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free), fetched from the network; no credential, import or --model needed
noLogin.note: Verified: with an empty home, `opencode run "reply ok"` started, defaulted to opencode/big-pickle (agent build) and answered. This matches the spec promise of no model required. `opencode auth list` prints 'No authenticated integrations'; `opencode auth export` prints [].

authExport.command: opencode auth export [<integration id or name>]   (prints to stdout, secrets included; no argument exports every integration)
authExport.shape: JSON array of { id: 'cred_<id>', integrationID, label, active: boolean, value }. value is { type: 'key', key } for API keys or { type: 'oauth', methodID, refresh, access, expires } for sign-in.
authExport.note: The key shape was exported from a real `auth login` (throwaway key). The oauth shape was verified by importing then re-exporting an invented credential: all tokens round-trip. See auth-export.sample.json (invented, canary strings). Not verified: a real ChatGPT sign-in file.

authImport.command: opencode auth import [<file>]   (reads stdin when omitted)
authImport.merge: Additive by credential id. A credential whose id already exists is skipped ('Imported 0 credentials, skipped 1 already present', the stored key is NOT overwritten even if the file carries a different one). A new id is added with active=false, even when the file says active=true, and the existing active credential for that integration stays active. So an import into a fresh pod home is exact; a token refreshed later in the CLI is never overwritten by re-importing the same file.
authImport.validation: Strict schema: errors name the missing key path (e.g. at [0]["value"]["methodID"])
authImport.fallback: Not needed: import is usable. The spec fallback (write the credential store directly) is not recorded as required; the store is SQLite, so writing it directly would be worse than importing.
authImport.note: A rotated auth_json (new tokens) imported over an old one with the same credential ids is skipped. If rotation reuses the id, Task 11 must use new ids or `opencode auth logout` before import; this is a caveat for the version-marker rule in the spec. Only `active` credentials are used by the run, so the adapter should import into a fresh home or verify with `auth list`.
authImport.forTask11: Rotation rule (verified twice): importing a file whose credential id already exists is skipped and keeps the old key, and importing a new id adds it with active=false while the old one stays active. To rotate, run `opencode auth logout <integration> <credentialId>` for every stored credential of that integration (the next remaining one becomes active, so logout all of them), then `opencode auth import`; or start from a fresh home on the per-run volume. Verified: after logging out the old id, importing the same file with the rotated key made it active.

service.effect: Writes {"disabled": true} to $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/service.json (verified). Commands accept --standalone (private server for that command) or --server <url>; without either they use the background service (opencode service start|stop|status). `opencode run --standalone` was verified: the CLI spawns its own `serve --stdio --port 0` child and exits with it. One pod therefore runs one private server using --standalone, or service.json disabled; both are verified to work, the TUI form (`opencode --standalone`) was not driven.
service.note: Auth commands (`auth list|export|import|login`) also need --standalone (or a running service).

configDelivery.note: OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT (inline JSON config) is read by the pinned release; verified end to end (provider, models, env). Also present in the binary: OPENCODE_CONFIG, OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR, OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE, OPENCODE_DISABLE_MODELS_FETCH, OPENCODE_DISABLE_FREE_MODELS, OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE*.

keys.models: provider.agentdesk.models: object keyed by model id, values may be {}; also provider.agentdesk.npm = package id

customProvider.selection: `--model agentdesk/org/model-a` selects model id 'org/model-a' under provider 'agentdesk' (the first slash splits, the rest stays one id); `opencode models` lists it as agentdesk/org/model-a. Verified: the request to the endpoint carried model 'org/model-a' and POST <baseURL>/chat/completions with SSE.

autoUpdate.note: The variable name is present in the binary and was exported in every run; no update call was observed. `opencode upgrade` exists as a command; the pod should also not run it.

status.mechanism: a plugin: a .js module in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/plugins/ (auto-loaded; also config plugin: [...]) with a default export { id, setup(ctx) }. ctx.event.subscribe({ types? }) returns an async iterable of events. The older `export const X = async () => ({ event })` form is rejected ('Plugin must export a default definition with an id and an effect or setup function').
status.payload: { id, created, type, data: { sessionID, ... }, durable?, location? }. See images/runner/test/fixtures/opencode-hooks/events.jsonl (ids and paths scrubbed).
status.mapping: plugin setup -> started, session.execution.started -> working, permission.asked -> needs_input, permission.replied -> working (reply once|always|reject), session.execution.succeeded|failed|interrupted -> idle, location.shutdown -> finished. Verified with a mock OpenAI-compatible server that answers with a tool call and OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT permission {bash: ask}: on a long-lived server (`opencode serve`) the run blocked for 11 s after permission.asked (data { id, sessionID, action: 'shell', resources: ['echo hi'], source: { type: 'tool', messageID, id } }) with no other event, then permission.replied (data { sessionID, requestID, reply }) arrived when POST /api/session/<id>/permission/<requestID>/reply { decision: 'once' } answered it and the run went on to session.execution.succeeded. In a non-interactive `opencode run` (no --auto) the request is auto-rejected within 1 ms (permission.asked, permission.replied reply 'reject', session.tool.failed error.type 'permission.rejected'), so a headless run never blocks; only the TUI or a server waits for a person. session.form.* (question/form tool) was not driven; a form prompt would map to needs_input the same way, to be confirmed in Task 10.
status.note: Subscribing needs an async for-await loop started from setup, not awaited. Events fixture: images/runner/test/fixtures/opencode-hooks/events.jsonl (the permission session is the second session, ses_002).

transcript.path: $XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode/opencode.db (SQLite: tables session_v*, session_message, session_part, event, ...). There is no JSONL file on disk.
transcript.format: Read it through the CLI: `opencode session export <id>` prints JSON { info: { id, model, cost, tokens, outcome, time, title, location }, messages: [ user { text, files }, assistant { agent, model, content[], finish, tokens }, idle { outcome } ] }. `opencode session list [--format json]` lists sessions. The fixture images/runner/test/fixtures/opencode-transcript/session.jsonl is that export, one object per line (info first).
transcript.note: The runner cannot tail a file like Claude or Codex; it should collect the plugin event stream into a JSONL file (the events fixture) and call `session export` at the end or on pause.

resume.command: opencode run -s <session id> "<message>"   (non-interactive; -c continues the last session); TUI: opencode --session <id> or opencode --continue

builtinModelsNote: From `opencode models` on 2026-11-25 with no login (11 free models, fetched online; list changes). Each id is provider-prefixed, so the picker value passes straight to --model. Task 8 should keep this short; modelOptional means a run with no model uses the CLI default (opencode/big-pickle).

modelList.appliesTo: api_key (own endpoint); auth_json has no known list endpoint, use builtinModels
modelList.answerShape: { object: 'list', data: [{ id, object, created, owned_by }] }, see models-ok.json. The CLI itself also called GET <baseURL>/models when it started with the custom provider (seen on the mock).

check.results: 200 with data array = ok; 401 with error.code invalid_api_key = rejected (real api.openai.com body, key scrubbed, see models-401.json; other OpenAI-compatible servers vary, so any 401/403 = rejected); anything else shaped differently = invalid (models-bad.json)

startupCheck.note: A plugin-driven start emits session.execution.started within about 100 ms of the first prompt; but with no initial prompt the TUI emits no session event until the user types, so an idle TUI could look like a silent start. The 5-minute needs_input startup check must count plugin setup (started) as the first signal, as for Claude and Codex.

parityNotes.watch: true: events come from a plugin, not a hook command, so the runner needs the plugin file written at start (Task 10). needs_input is verified: permission.asked fires while a prompt blocks the run and permission.replied fires when it is answered.
parityNotes.attach: true with a note: the TUI under tmux was not driven in this spike; `opencode run` and --standalone were verified.
parityNotes.pauseResume: true: sessions persist in opencode.db on the per-run volume; `opencode run -s <id>` resumed by id (listed, exported). Credentials live in the same database, so token rotation follows the version-marker rule: a re-import of the same credential ids is skipped, see authImport.note.

notes: Verified end to end against a local mock OpenAI-compatible server with a throwaway key, plus the real opencode.ai free models (no login) and a real api.openai.com 401 body.

Not verified: a real ChatGPT/OAuth sign-in, the interactive TUI and the session.form.* question tool. Verified later in a second run: a tool call that needs permission (permission.asked / permission.replied).
Every parity value is true; the notes above are caveats for Tasks 8, 10, 11 and 13, none is a missing capability, so the gate does not stop the plan.
